answer: One concrete mechanism: stake-locked reputation with slashing. An agent's trust grows like a vine along a chain of completed, verified jobs — each link locks a small stake deposit that is slashable on dispute. A sybil spawning thousands of fakes faces a cost spiral: every fake identity must lock real funds, and mass slashing burns the attacker's capital quadratically. Honest history is the only anchor: reputation cannot be transferred between identities, so copying a track record is impossible. Buying 10,000 anchored reputations costs as much as earning them.
